Thanks — quick answers below that I recommend we send back to John: 

- Cloud providers / subprocessors: Primary compute & model hosting: GCP (us-west1) and AWS (us-east-1) depending on customer region and private tenant configuration. Secondary services: Datadog (monitoring), Sentry (error reporting), SendGrid (transactional email) — these are listed in the attached CSV.
- Data boundaries: Redwood processes request text to generate model outputs; we do not persist request texts beyond the short-term KV cache used for inference. For hosted customers, request logs are retained for 30 days by default for debugging and billing, and can be configured shorter or disabled for dedicated/private customers. Logs may contain user-provided text; customer-configured redaction + private deployments remove PII retention.
- PII in logs: It is possible if the customer sends PII in requests. We provide redaction tools and recommend customers not send PHI in hosted mode unless covered by a signed BAA / private deployment.
- SOC 2: We completed readiness and have a SOC 2 Type II audit in progress — expected report delivery Q3 2026 (target: 2026-08-31). The SOC2_summary_redwood_v2.pdf is the interim summary and control map.
- HIPAA / PHI: We support HIPAA for private deployments with a BAA; hosted customers can discuss a BAA with the account team and respective controls/contract addendum.

Next steps I suggest we take before replying to Acme: 
1) Attach the CSV and the SOC2 summary (already attached).
2) Provide the short data-boundary paragraph below for their questionnaire.
3) Offer a 30-min technical sync with me and an engineer this week.

Suggested data-boundary paragraph to paste into questionnaire:
"Redwood Inference processes customer-provided input to produce inference outputs. For hosted deployments, transient request data is buffered during inference and request logs are retained for 30 days by default for debugging and billing. Customers can configure log retention to 0 days or elect Dedicated/Private deployments where logs and model artifacts are isolated to customer-controlled infrastructure. Persistent storage of model weights or outputs is not performed unless explicitly configured by the customer. Third-party subprocessors used for monitoring and email (e.g., Datadog, SendGrid) receive only telemetry or transactional metadata; they do not receive full model weights or production artifacts."

I can send this back to John + security and propose Tue/Wed for the sync.
